description: Translation glossary for QuantEcon lectures (English to Malayalam). Validated by the native-speaker packet reply 2026-08-03 (experiments/ml-benchmark/DISPOSITIONS.md): C1 confirmed keep-English for the 34 most frequent unpinned terms — deliberately NOT pinned, the policy holds unpinned (203/203 terms measured) — and C2/A8 pinned the software-interface verbs (click, option, set, type, press) that machine output had transliterated; terminology extractors never propose interface verbs, so nothing else protects them. Policy: keep-English-dominant — technical/domain terms keep their English form (ml == en), and ordinary English content words (everyday adjectives, adverbs, nouns) also usually stay in Latin script per packet A1; Malayalam is generated mainly as grammatical connective tissue around the English words. The few translated 'everyday' entries below (country, year, ...) are deliberate exceptions with a natural in-use equivalent, not an open class to extend. Where ml == en, the term is intentionally kept in English. Malayalam values for the everyday words are taken from native-speaker reviewer Adisankar Manoj Thanuja's worked examples. Grammatical function words (we, two, each, more, before, ...) are deliberately NOT pinned here: they inflect with Malayalam grammar and are handled by the prose rules in language-config, not term-level consistency.
